Answer: A
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, curvilinear calcification along the inferior and anterior border of the cardiac silhouette, which is characteristic of a calcified left ventricular aneurysm. This specific location and morphology distinguish it from pericardial calcifications (which typically outline the entire heart or are located posteriorly/inferiorly without this focal bulge) or valvular/annular calcifications.
